paraphrase: Depositors and/or speech communities acting as collection Owners consider access requests, while the terms also recognise decisions by resource controllers; the documents do not say how they share the decision. AILLA decides when the depositor cannot be contacted or is no longer available to respond.
short_quote: The Restricted setting should only be used in situations in which the depositor, the speech community, and/or some other person or organization is willing to control access to the content of the set.
section: AILLA-07: 2.6.1 Visibility Settings, Restricted (p. 12), and 2.6.2.2 Rights and Use Note (p. 14); AILLA-06: 2(c); AILLA-05: clause 7 and opening paragraph
note: Reason: The Restricted instructions require Owners to consider and answer requests without requiring them to grant access, and expressly identify depositors and/or speech communities as possible Owners. Resource controllers have general access authority, and AILLA staff decide when the depositor is unavailable. general statement. Rule 19: the Owner holders are identified explicitly in the access-control passage, not inferred from the role; Owners and resource controllers are not expressly equated. Rule 3: the community interests considered by AILLA under clause 7 do not themselves confer a further decision. partly deferred: the licence's opening paragraph leaves specific access conditions to the attached AILLA Metadata Sheet (rules 17 and 21). Resolved on 2026-11-16; see differences.csv. fallback: AILLA decides only when the depositor cannot be contacted or is no longer available (rule 22).

paraphrase: A person requesting takedown or review is asked to provide their own reasons for removing or reviewing material. The documents do not specify a format for depositors' reasons when initially setting an access level.
short_quote: the reason for why you think the material should be taken down or reviewed
section: Takedown Policy > Please provide the information detailed below
note: Reason: The takedown policy asks the requesting party to supply reasons in their own words and supplies no closed list of reasons. Rule 8 applies to a party providing reasons for a restriction, and rule 20 recognises takedown protection or removal as a restriction. This applies to the takedown route; the access requester's reasons in ELAR-01 concern obtaining access and are not used as evidence for GR1. Resolved on 2026-11-16; see differences.csv. Scope: the takedown route only.

paraphrase: The archive restricts commercial and other uses outside private research or education, copying and onward dissemination, uploads to web-based systems, AI or machine learning use without community consent, and automated collection. It also prohibits uses causing disparagement, disrespect, reputational damage or harm to individuals or groups.
short_quote: I will not knowingly use materials for any purpose which causes disparagement, disrespect, damage to reputation, or harm to any individual or group.
section: ELAR-04: Terms and Conditions and Data Protection Statement > condition 8; ELAR-01: Artificial Intelligence Use and conditions 3-5; ELAR-02: Conditions of Access and Use of ELAR holdings
note: Reason: The archive's conditions explicitly name restricted purposes and prohibited harms, which are coded as grounds named by the archive under rule 8. These statements do not identify the reasons for particular Subscriber Access settings. archive-initiated. partly deferred: specific restrictions accompany each item (ELAR-01 and ELAR-02; rules 17 and 21). No cultural sensitivity or other unstated reason is inferred. Resolved on 2026-11-16; see differences.csv. conditions of use (rule 23). The reasons for restricting a particular bundle are left to the record of that bundle (ELAR-01, FAQ).

paraphrase: The documents name Indigenous cultural protocols, protection of intellectual property and copyright, creators' privacy, and failure to meet accessibility requirements as grounds for limiting access. AILLA requires Login Required visibility when files do not meet the stated accessibility standard. The conditions of use that AILLA sets for all users also count: no commercial use, no alteration and no derived works without legal authorisation, respect for intellectual property, copyright and cultural protocols, and anonymity of creators where the metadata requires it.
short_quote: If you are unable to meet the requirements for WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines, please do not use the Public visibility setting, even if the media files are licensed under Creative Commons.
section: AILLA-07: 2.6.1 Visibility Settings, Public (p. 11), and 2.6.2.2 Rights and Use Note (p. 14); AILLA-09: Mission #2: Accessibility; AILLA-08: AILLA Terms & Conditions of Use, opening paragraph; AILLA-05: opening paragraph; AILLA-06: 1(a) to 1(d) and 3
note: Reason: The deposit instructions connect accessibility requirements to a mandatory login setting, the mission links registration to intellectual property and privacy protection, and the repository terms name cultural protection. These are named grounds, not a closed list of depositor choices. archive-initiated: the accessibility requirement and the mission's explanation of registration concern restrictions required by AILLA. partly deferred: file-specific explanations belong in the Rights and Use Note, and the licence leaves specific access conditions to the attached Metadata Sheet (rules 17 and 21). conditions of use: added at resolution on 2026-11-16 under rule 23; the code did not change.

paraphrase: The documents name ceremonial or gender restrictions, sensitive genealogy, photographs or recordings of deceased people, and the interests and sensitivities of relevant communities. They also name cultural sensitivity, infringement of rights, privacy, defamation, copyright and other legal concerns as grounds for the archive's restrictions or takedown route. The conditions of use that PARADISEC sets for all users also count: use only for private scholarly research or education and not for profit, no copying or distribution to third parties, no use of the data in commercial products or in models, and no upload to web-based systems that keep the data.
short_quote: Please state whether any special conditions should be considered when handling this material, e.g. ceremonial or gender restricted material, sensitive genealogical material, photographs or recordings of deceased people:
